goal: Let a Full Access admin connect Netskope to both pull Netskope-sourced signals into a user's Dune risk score and, optionally, push Dune-derived risk signals back into Netskope's User Confidence Index for its own enforcement.
constraints: Netskope licensing varies per client tenant (base SSE tier vs. separately licensed Advanced UEBA for User Confidence Index)
Netskope's data model is user-keyed via SCIM/SSO, unlike CrowdStrike's device-keyed model, so mapping is structurally simpler
RBAC currently offers no admin persona narrower than Full Access, a gap now recurring for a second security-tooling integration
Existing risk score recompute follows a scheduled cadence, not real-time
A second vendor now blends into the same risk score as CrowdStrike, introducing a cross-vendor normalization and correlation problem that did not exist with one integration
Write-back to Netskope's UCI requires write-scoped API credentials, a materially larger security review surface than read-only ingestion
assumptions: Single blended overall score and IAM-identity-based mapping are confirmed, carried over from the CrowdStrike precedent for consistency
End users should see only a summary of what drives their score, not raw Netskope detail
Weight changes apply on the next scheduled sync rather than instantly

Behavior Confidence (UCI) and the five granular categories may both be enabled at once (soft-warned, not blocked), except when Share Risk Signals is active, in which case Behavior Confidence is force-disabled to prevent a circular scoring dependency
gaps: Cross-vendor signal correlation (CrowdStrike and Netskope both reporting the same real-world event) is unaddressed
No combined normalization scheme across UCI's native scale, Netskope category severities, and CrowdStrike's category scores
No remediation path described for a user disputing a Dune signal already pushed to and consumed by Netskope
No stated security review process for write-back's expanded credential scope and third-party enforcement influence
No employee-facing disclosure update described for the new data source, now higher-stakes since Dune data also flows outward
No success metric or rollout signal defined, same unresolved gap as CrowdStrike, now overdue across two integrations
Capability re-detection and multi-tenant support unconfirmed, same open question as CrowdStrike, now recurring
edge_cases: Netskope and CrowdStrike syncs both failing in the same window with no combined degraded-state view
A user simultaneously flagged 'No Endpoint Visibility' and 'No Netskope Visibility'
Behavior Confidence enabled before UBA data has populated for a new tenant
Admin attempts to enable Share Risk Signals while Behavior Confidence is active — force-disabled, not just warned
A push to Netskope's UCI Impact endpoint fails mid-cycle, distinct from an ingestion sync failure
Admin disables Share Risk Signals after active use — already-pushed data cannot be retracted from Netskope's own scoring model
Re-linking a mismatched Netskope user mapping is not restated even though the equivalent CrowdStrike behavior exists

critical_questions.question: When CrowdStrike and Netskope both report signals traceable to the same real-world event for one user, should the blended score dampen, deduplicate, or allow compounding?
What is the combined normalization method across UCI's native scale, Netskope category severities, and CrowdStrike's category scores?
What security review is required before write-back ships, given Dune's risk data now directly influences a third-party system's access-control enforcement?
What is the remediation path if a user disputes a Dune risk signal that has already been pushed to and consumed by Netskope?
Is there a defined success signal for this feature, now overdue across two risk-signal integrations?
Does capability re-detection and multi-tenant support need to be solved generically across both integrations rather than per-vendor?

design_risks: Write-back materially raises the trust and security stakes of this feature beyond CrowdStrike's consume-only precedent — Dune is no longer just displaying a score, it is now feeding a third party's enforcement decisions
A second vendor doubles the surface area for score opacity and for two vendors independently penalizing the same incident

Soft-warning the UCI/granular overlap normalizes double-counting for ingestion, even though the equivalent write-back combination was judged serious enough to hard-block — worth revisiting whether the ingestion-only overlap deserves the same treatment

Irreversibility of pushed signals (Dune cannot retract data Netskope has already consumed) needs to be surfaced clearly in the UI, not just documented in edge-cases.md, or admins will assume disabling the feature is a clean rollback
teaching_notes: Treat crowdstrike-integration/design-strategy.md as the primary layout reference; reuse the settings page, category weight sliders, and score breakdown section directly rather than reinventing for Netskope
knowledge/features/rbac/prd.json's open Super Admin question now has a second forcing function; this raises its priority rather than introducing a new consideration
Netskope's UCI scale (1-1000, lower = riskier) is inverted relative to Dune's own risk score convention (higher = riskier) — never surface a raw UCI number without translating direction
Reuse the CrowdStrike 'who will this affect' live preview pattern rather than designing a second, differently-shaped preview

Share Risk Signals is a net-new flow shape (outbound data configuration) that has no precedent elsewhere in Dune's product — design-strategist should treat it as a distinct pattern, not force it into the inbound weighting UI's shape
